title: "Routine maintenance and CI"
description: "Update schemas, run thin maintenance commands, inspect reports, and publish client docs."
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Routine maintenance and CI}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Use the same loop for new and existing clients: **update inputs -> plan -> review
-> apply -> check -> test -> commit**. Schemas, service policy, callbacks, fixed
fixtures, output, `.specmill/helpers/`, and `.specmill/manifest.json` form one
reviewed change. For a toolkit upgrade, follow the
[existing-client upgrade workflow](existing-clients.html#update-an-already-configured-client).
Normal generation does not update client-owned request helpers or session controls.

## 1. Review schema changes

Keep the old schema snapshot while downloading the new one using your client's
own acquisition process. Use the same filename and selection policy for both
versions. For example, place `catalogue.json` in `schema-before/` and `schema-after/`:

```{r compare, eval=FALSE}
selection <- list(methods = c('GET', 'POST'), exclude = '^/internal/')
diff <- specmill::schema_diff(
  '/path/to/schema-before', '/path/to/schema-after',
  policies = list('catalogue.json' = selection)
)
cat(specmill::format_diff_markdown(diff))
specmill::count_diff_changes(diff)
```

`schema_diff()` compares method/path identities and canonical data including
reachable local references and response shapes. Changed contracts enter the
breaking-change report lane conservatively for review. Parsing failures stop
comparison. These labels do not prove runtime compatibility.

For parsed operation records, `compare_operations(old, new)` gives a smaller
report of additions, removals, changed parameters/bodies, and unknown response
compatibility. Unsupported operations remain parser diagnostics, so review them
alongside any comparison.

Compare schema revisions under a fixed policy, then review policy changes
separately. Otherwise, changing an exclusion can look like an upstream deletion.
Generation does not automatically delete an implementation merely because an
operation disappears from an unsupported or changed schema. Eligible removal
comes from explicit exclusions or reconciled renames and requires verified ownership.

Naming conventions are proposal-time settings. `generate_client()` uses the
explicit service YAML names and does not reapply `name_case`. To propose names
for new endpoints, run `configure_client(..., name_case = 'snake_case')`, review
its changes, and copy the accepted mappings into the existing YAML.

## 2. Generate and verify

```{r loop, eval=FALSE}
root <- normalizePath('/path/to/client', winslash = '/', mustWork = TRUE)
plan <- specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan')
plan$files
plan$drift
plan$diagnostics
plan$validation
# After reviewing the change:
specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'apply')
specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'check')
testthat::test_local(root, stop_on_failure = TRUE)
```

Generation validates each schema locally against its official OpenAPI JSON
Schema before translating operations. Invalid documents and unsupported coverage
block apply and check; inspect `plan$validation` for the full findings.
References outside the document must be bundled first.

Check mode warns when a current schema's hash differs from the last applied
manifest, showing its path and previous/current SHA-256 hashes. The warning
appears before schema translation, including when the changed schema cannot be
translated. A schema newly referenced by existing configuration reports its
previous hash as `not recorded`. Initial generation and legacy manifests without
input hashes have no comparison baseline. Check writes no client files; use
plan mode to review file changes, then apply reviewed output to record the new
baseline. A hash change alone does not mean a function needs rebuilding.

When the manifest has an endpoint inventory, the warning also lists added and
removed method/path pairs, identifies additions outside current selection policy,
and names previously configured functions affected by removals. It appears even
when a removed endpoint makes a function mapping invalid. For a parseable plan,
the same information is in `plan$schema_changes` and its printed summary.
This compares endpoint presence; it does not classify parameter or response
changes as compatible or breaking. Removed endpoints never authorize deleting
client functions automatically.

An upgrade from a manifest containing only hashes needs one reviewed apply to
record the endpoint inventory. Plan/check report that comparison is unavailable
until the inventory exists. Schema files removed from configuration or renamed
are not automatically matched to their previous versions. Commit the updated
manifest with the reviewed policy and generated output.

This warning runs only when the generation check is called. It does not download
schemas or automatically attach to `devtools::build()` or `devtools::check()`.
Include the generation check in your project's development command or CI as
shown below.

Supply the same explicit `callbacks` environment on each call when your policy
uses callbacks. Run the relevant manual/helper tests too. Reapplying unchanged
inputs should produce only unchanged/retained file actions. Review output diffs
before committing; do not hand-edit generated files to fix a policy error.

### Defer a changed contract that does not validate yet

By default every selected operation must validate, and one failing operation
blocks apply and check. When an upstream revision breaks one operation, you can
defer that single contract revision instead of excluding the operation or
forgetting its inventory. Enrollment is explicit and is recorded on apply only.
For a worked example with real output, see
[Defer or skip an operation](deferral.html):

```{r defer, eval=FALSE}
enroll <- list(enroll = c('demo GET /bad' = 'Response lacks a description'))
specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan', deferrals = enroll)
specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'apply', deferrals = enroll)
```

The key is `<service id> <METHOD> <path>`; the reason is one line. The manifest
stores the reason, source, operation key, and a `v1:` SHA-256 fingerprint of the
operation, its path-level parameters and servers, security, host/base path, and
every transitively referenced local definition (sorted keys, normalized line
endings). Healthy operations generate normally.

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `deferred` | Fingerprint unchanged. Skipped; apply and check are no-ops. |
| `retry_blocked` | Contract changed but still fails. Needs a fix, a new enrollment, or an opt-in policy. |
| `retry_recovered` | Contract changed and now passes. Plan shows the wrapper; apply writes it through the normal gates and drops the enrollment. |
| `uncertain` | Enrollment metadata, source, or operation cannot be read or matched. The record is kept untouched and the operation stays withheld; check fails until you clear or re-enroll it. A record that is not an object cannot be matched, so apply stays strict for it. |

Clearing is an explicit retry: `deferrals = list(clear = 'demo GET /bad')`. A
toolkit update alone, key order, whitespace, and edits to unrelated operations or
definitions do not wake an enrollment; prose changes inside the contract do.
Fingerprints are scoped per source, so equal paths in other APIs are unaffected.

To enroll failures of listed diagnostic codes without a manual step, add
`deferral: {automatic: [schema_validation_invalid]}` to the service. Other codes,
document-level findings, and shared blockers (an unreadable schema, a bad
policy) still stop the run. Validation is never disabled.

Plan and check are read-only. Deferral never deletes code: an existing wrapper,
its documentation, tests and ownership are preserved, including a function inside
a grouped file that a healthy sibling rewrites. A never-generated deferred
operation gets no placeholder. A project whose operations are all deferred still
persists the enrollment, and repeating an empty apply is a no-op.

### Prune retired output

Preserving output is the default; removal is opt-in. To retire an operation,
defer or exclude it so it is no longer generated, then name it:

```{r prune, eval=FALSE}
specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan', prune = 'demo GET /bad')
specmill::generate_client(root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'apply', prune = 'demo GET /bad')
```

Apply removes the operation's R file, tests and help page, regenerates
`NAMESPACE` (when documentation is generated) and drops the ownership records.
The ID is matched against manifest ownership, so it may name a service that was
since removed from `specmill.yml`; an enrolled deferral ID also matches the
retired owner of the same `METHOD /path`. Otherwise the service in the ID must
be the owner the manifest records, which can differ from the service you
remember generating the file from: copy the ID from `files[<path>].operations` in
`.specmill/manifest.json`. Pruning refuses an operation that is
still generated, an ID that owns nothing, and a file shared with other
operations. A hand-edited file is retained, as with any removal. Without
`prune`, outputs of a removed service stay in place with their old ownership
record.

Named prune covers the selected `artifacts`.

A manifest file path also works, e.g. `prune = 'R/helper_preflight.R'`. It drops
that file and its ownership record whole, which is the way to clear a stale
entry that owns no operations (a helper whose file is already gone). It refuses
a still-generated `R/` or `tests/` file and `NAMESPACE`; an edited file is retained.

### Review a clean regeneration

Before pruning, `regeneration_report()` shows what a full rebuild would add,
change or remove, and what Specmill leaves alone. It writes nothing:

```{r report, eval=FALSE}
specmill::regeneration_report(root, config = 'specmill.yml')
```

Each file gets a category: `added`, `changed`, `unchanged`, `edited_conflict`
and `unowned_collision` (a hand-written file at a generated path), `kept`
(lifecycle badge, existing implementation, deferral or `NAMESPACE`),
`would_remove` (owned but no longer generated; `prune_eligible` is `FALSE` when
an edit makes `prune` refuse it, and `reason` notes a removed service),
`unowned_generated` (generated-looking, no ownership record) and `hand_written`
(left alone, so the remainder is your hand-built inventory). It compares the
in-memory plan with the current tree rather than purging and rebuilding:
deferrals, existing implementations and lifecycle badges keep their placement.

`prune = 'all'` plans removal of every manifest-owned, unmodified output so a
project can be regenerated from scratch; unowned and edited files are untouched.
It ignores `spec`, `config`, `validation`, `artifacts`, `adopt` and `deferrals`.
Apply asks `Are you sure? [y/N]` (default no). Non-interactive sessions never
prompt: pass `confirm = TRUE`, or the call aborts without writing.

Limitations: a contract that stays broken needs a human decision; fingerprints
cover local references only; a renamed source or removed operation is reported as
`uncertain` rather than matched.

## 3. Add a thin sourceable command

Save the following as `dev/generate.R` in a client without an existing command:

```r
.client_root <- specmill::script_root('generate.R')
generate_main <- function(root = .client_root, args = commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)) {
  specmill::generation_command(root, args = args, kind = 'stubs')
}
if (sys.nframe() == 0L) generate_main()
```

`script_root()` locates the package from the source frame or Rscript invocation,
so the command works from another working directory. Add explicit callback
loading inside `generate_main()` if needed, as in the existing-client guide.
Source it in R and call `generate_main(args = '--plan')`, or run:

```sh
Rscript dev/generate.R --plan
Rscript dev/generate.R --check
Rscript dev/generate.R
```

The final command **applies**. Compatibility commands intentionally have a
different default from the core `generate_client()`, which defaults to check.

| Command kind | Preview | Check | Apply |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stubs` (wrappers and documentation) | `--plan` | `--check` | No mode flag |
| `tests` (fixed contract tests) | `--dry-run` | `--check` | `--generate` or no mode flag |

`--help` describes accepted flags. The stubs command accepts legacy
`--rebuild=<prefix>` flags, and the tests command accepts `--force`. Both are
ignored with a warning: YAML controls selection, and ownership is never
overridden. Check/apply test commands
fail if any selected operation lacks a fixed contract. Plan can report the gaps.

For custom orchestration, use `generate_client(artifacts = ...)` to limit
reconciliation to `wrappers`, `tests`, or `documentation`. Shared ownership and
manifest checks still apply.

## 4. Inspect implementation and test gaps

```{r inspect, eval=FALSE}
inspection <- specmill::inspect_client(root)
inspection$coverage
inspection$manual_exports
inspection$diagnostics
inspection$helpers
inspection$protected_sources
```

Coverage counts files and declarations, not passing tests or working endpoints.
Selected unsupported operations remain in totals. Manual exported wrappers are
separate from the schema denominator and still need their own tests.

For badges and baseline comparisons, create a separate client report policy:

```yaml
# dev/coverage.yml
baseline: dev/coverage-baseline.json
groups:
  catalogue:
    services: '^catalogue$'
    label: Catalogue wrappers
    badge: man/figures/catalogue-coverage.json
```

By default a group counts only the operations your policy selected, so a client
that wraps everything it selected reads 100% however much of the API that is. To
measure coverage of the API itself, opt a group in to the schema as its
denominator:

```yaml
groups:
  catalogue:
    services: '^catalogue$'
    label: Catalogue wrappers
    badge: man/figures/catalogue-coverage.json
    denominator: schema          # default: selected
    exclude: ['^GET /health']    # optional: operations you skip on purpose
```

With `denominator: schema` the total is every operation in the schemas the
matched services reference, including those your selection policy excludes, minus
any operation whose `METHOD /path` matches an `exclude` regex (the same regex
engine as `selection.exclude`). An operation counts once per `METHOD /path` in the
group, however many schema files or services describe it, so `-full` and
`-rebuild` services, or a route that two schema files both document, do not
double count. Keep one API surface in a group: two APIs on different servers that
share a route would count as one, so put them in separate groups. An operation is
covered when any service of the group wraps it. A path item that cannot be parsed
counts as one operation named `PATH /path`. The badge, baseline and GitHub
outputs keep their format; `endpoints` is the schema total and `functions` the
wrapped count.

Each schema-mode group prints how many schema operations have no wrapper and how
many of those are not selected. `coverage_report()` returns the full list as
`gaps`, one data frame per group with `key`, `schema`, `status` (`excluded`,
`unsupported`, `selected`, ...) and `services`, so the gap can be acted on:

```{r gaps, eval=FALSE}
report <- specmill::coverage_report(root, file.path(root, 'dev/coverage.yml'))
report$gaps$catalogue
```

Group `services` values are regex strings matching service IDs. Groups must
partition every configured service exactly once. Create the baseline's parent
directory before apply. Report-policy filenames passed as strings are resolved
by R against the working directory; make them explicit with `file.path(root, ...)`:

```{r reports, eval=FALSE}
specmill::coverage_report(root, file.path(root, 'dev/coverage.yml'))
specmill::coverage_report(root, file.path(root, 'dev/coverage.yml'), mode = 'apply')
specmill::test_gap_report(root, list(
  helpers = list('api_request'), report_dir = 'dev/test-gaps',
  readiness_report = 'dev/readiness-report.json'
))
```

Reports default to read-only plans. Coverage apply writes badges and its baseline;
gap-report apply writes a dated JSON report. Gap reasons distinguish missing
contracts, absent/empty test files, and unsupported operations. `readiness_report`
is a pointer to your canonical audit, not an audit created by this call.

## 5. Add client-specific checks to CI

CI should install the project's reviewed toolkit and formatter, then run
generation checks before tests. For a client with no callbacks, an R CI step can be:

```r
checked <- specmill::generate_client('.', config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'check')
stopifnot(length(checked$diagnostics) == 0L)
testthat::test_local('.', stop_on_failure = TRUE)
```

If you intentionally retain unsupported operations, use an explicit reviewed
diagnostic allowance instead of removing the diagnostics gate. Do not use
`continue-on-error` for invalid configuration or schema parsing before publishing
generated output. Generation commands write existing summary keys to
`GITHUB_OUTPUT` when that environment variable is set; core functions return
structured results and errors instead of choosing a process exit code.

`check_public_boundary()` accepts your forbidden host/file/export/schema regexes
and approved manual-export list. `check_client_hooks()` validates supplied runtime
hook declarations against parsed client definitions. Their reference pages explain
arguments and return values. Keep these policies client-specific.

`credential_status()` and `credential_preflight()` detect absent/placeholder
credentials without logging values or making requests. They cannot prove a key
is authorized. Offline generation and fixed contract tests need no live key.

### Gate an upstream schema publication

A publisher can use `read_operations()` directly on the candidate local schema,
without a client project or generated files. Save this as an R script and invoke
it with `Rscript validate-schema.R candidate.json` using a reviewed specmill pin:

```r
files <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(files) > 0L)
for (file in files) {
  parsed <- specmill::read_operations(file)
  for (d in parsed$diagnostics) cat(file, d$code, d$key, '\n')
  stopifnot(length(parsed$diagnostics) == 0L)
}
```

Parsing errors and failed assertions exit unsuccessfully. Publish only after
this step succeeds. Do not apply client selection filters to a whole-schema
gate: excluded operations are inventoried but not validated. This gate rejects
both detected schema defects and specmill capability gaps. It is not a complete
OpenAPI conformance validator or proof of a working service. Fixture and server
diagnostics are separate results and need separate gates if required.

For the AMOS `GET /api/amos/get_similar_structures/{identifier_type}/{identifier}`
declaration containing only a `dtxsid` path parameter, the reader reports three
schema defects: unmatched `dtxsid`, missing `identifier_type`, and missing
`identifier`. Each diagnostic has the same stable method/path `key`, a `source`
file, and a `source_location` JSON Pointer. The unmatched declaration points to
its parameter object; missing declarations point to the path item, since their
parameter objects do not exist. Use the full diagnostics list for all findings;
`inventory` keeps one row per operation and its first diagnostic for compatibility.
Earlier parsing errors can still prevent the path-name checks from running.

Generation plans expose these diagnostics too. Check and apply reject a mixed
selection containing this route before writing output. After reviewing the
findings, explicitly select independently supported routes to generate those.
A generated client mapping cannot repair malformed path metadata. Existing
`implementation: existing` support can retain a reviewed handwritten function
with a complete client contract, but does not certify or correct the schema.

## 6. Build documentation for your generated client

Set `documentation: true` and write useful `docs` policy before building the
client site. Generation stages roxygen and reconciles `man/` and `NAMESPACE`;
the help pages then become pkgdown reference pages. Add human-written vignettes
for authentication, common workflows, result interpretation, and errors.

From the **client package root**, install the documentation tools and initialize
pkgdown once:

```{r client-site, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c('pkgdown', 'usethis', 'rmarkdown', 'knitr'))
usethis::use_pkgdown()
pkgdown::build_site(preview = FALSE)
```

For a GitHub-hosted client, `usethis::use_pkgdown_github_pages()` configures the
publishing workflow and Pages settings. Review the generated workflow for your
default branch. See [usethis's pkgdown setup](https://usethis.r-lib.org/reference/use_pkgdown.html).

Keep its README short: purpose, installation, one example, and links to guides.
Put sequential workflows in vignettes and per-function detail in reference docs.
Render examples offline; mark real API calls `eval=FALSE` or use fixed examples
that do not contact services.

For **specmill's own site**, `_pkgdown.yml` defines navigation and
`.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml` builds on pull requests and publishes through
GitHub Actions Pages after default-branch pushes or manual dispatch. Local build command:

```{r specmill-site, eval=FALSE}
pkgdown::build_site(preview = FALSE)
```

Open `docs/index.html` after building. Site output is ignored by Git and package
builds; source articles and help pages are tracked. The workflow follows the
[r-lib pkgdown example](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/v2/examples/pkgdown.yaml).
